issues: The stable_reporting_period check imposes an unspecified numeric representation. Its regex does not recognize valid representations of 7 such as 07.00 or 0.7e1. A conforming implementation using either format could pass the numeric checks but fail this cadence check. Use a format-independent observation or omit this assertion and disclose the cadence coverage gap.

The cadence check treats delay(500) in every loop as a requirement for matching serial reports to occur every 500±100ms. The requirement specifies the delay, not a maximum total loop duration or serial-output length. Reporting and other permitted loop work can add time. Remove the unsupported upper interval bound unless an explicit report-period bound is supplied.
coverage_gaps: Independent numeric-presence checks do not establish correct X/Y/Z association or that all three values belong to the same sample.
The zero-acceleration scenario requires only one matching zero, not three zero-valued axis results.
The checks do not verify that output communicates acceleration units.
Successful sensor initialization is exercised, but initialization-failure handling, actual library selection, and I2C transaction correctness are not independently verified.
Serial timing observations do not establish that delay(500) executes in every loop.
reason: The reference implementation logically implements the required successful-initialization behavior: it uses the requested libraries, initializes serial at 9600 baud and the MPU6050 over the Uno's default A4/A5 I2C pins, prints the exact ready message, reads fresh acceleration events in m/s², reports all three axes, and delays 500ms each loop. The supplied ground-pin descriptions refer to the common ground net and introduce no behavioral conflict. Dynamic-input coverage is useful and honestly partial, but the cadence assertion can reject conforming implementations through unsupported formatting and timing restrictions.
